phase_name: Permission Broker Production Consumption Operational Hardening Independent Verification
summary: Independently verified 148G.1's PBPC-001 v1.2 operational hardening (F-148F-1, F-148F-3 closure) without trusting 148G.1's own tests, docstrings, or closure claims. Reconstructed the exact src/pcae/commands/push.py diff introduced by 148G.1 via git diff 06611796..90e7eb6e, classifying every hunk (SNAPSHOT_TYPE, DECISION_STATE_OBSERVATION, BROKER_FAILURE_BOUNDARY, FINAL_FRESHNESS_VALIDATION, ORDINARY_PATH_WIRING, STAGED_PATH_WIRING, DIAGNOSTIC -- zero UNRELATED hunks). Independently re-derived PBPC-001 v1.2 Section 17 (PBPC-REQ-059-061) from contract text rather than citing 148G.1's own requirement table; confirmed the four re-observed decision-bound fields (HEAD, branch, unpushed-commit count, active task ID) are exactly what PBPC-REQ-059's own text requires. Directly inspected _PushDecisionSnapshot: confirmed frozen/immutable (attempted mutation raises), in-process-only (never persisted), and not reused across attempts (two independently-observed snapshots for two different states are distinct). Confirmed snapshot capture timing (before PermissionBroker() construction and .evaluate(), both side-effect-free/pure) correctly represents decision-bound state. Confirmed both dispatch paths (ordinary and --staged-file-aware) call _evaluate_push_permission, _validate_push_permission_freshness, and their respective real git-push dispatch exactly twice each (source-level independent count), with no meaningful I/O between a passing freshness check and dispatch on either path. Added a new, independently-authored 19-test adversarial suite (tests/test_phase_148g2_permission_broker_operational_hardening_independent_verification.py) that does not extend or import 148G.1's own suite, covering angles 148G.1's own report did not claim: isolated unpushed-commit-count drift (not combined with any other fact change); final re-observation *helper failure* (a git command itself raising, not just a value drifting) for both HEAD and branch lookups, verified to fail closed; the new HEAD-observation empty-string fallback verified to not be mistaken for a match against a real decision-time HEAD; direct non-CLI unit tests of _PushDecisionSnapshot and _validate_push_permission_freshness; broker construction failure forced through the real pcae push CLI entrypoint (main(["push"])) on both dispatch paths, independent of 148F's rewritten tests, with retry-safety confirmed after a transient failure; canonical request field preservation (action_type/execution_class/requested_component/requested_capability/approval_present/simulation_only) and POL-004/POL-005 non-applicability/pass-through re-confirmed directly against Foundation source; HARD_BLOCK_REGISTRY independently recounted at 12; and a corrected consumer-scope guard check. F-148F-1: CLOSED -- INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (construction failure fails closed with exit code 1, zero dispatch, controlled diagnostic, on both paths; retry after transient failure succeeds normally with no partial state). F-148F-3: CLOSED -- INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED (all four fields correctly re-observed and compared; drift in any single field including unpushed-count in isolation, or multiple fields simultaneously, reliably blocks dispatch; a genuine non-forged broker ALLOW cannot dispatch after drift; PBPC-REQ-061's fresh-cycle semantics -- no automatic in-place re-evaluation, a fresh pcae push performs a genuinely fresh evaluate() call -- independently reconfirmed). One NON-BLOCKING finding: 148G.1's repaired 148C.10 consumer-scope guard test (test_push_module_is_the_authorized_pbpc_production_consumer) inspects pcae.commands.agent (a thin CLI wrapper containing no git-push dispatch call of its own) instead of pcae.core.agent, where the real push_file_changes/_run_git_push dispatch site independently lives -- not currently exploitable (pcae.core.agent independently confirmed to contain zero PermissionBroker/permission_broker_foundation references today), but the existing guard would not detect a future broker-bypass wired directly into the correct module; pcae.commands.phase, by contrast, is correctly targeted by the same test (it does contain both of that module's real dispatch calls). Two OBSERVATION-level findings, both low practical severity: (1) the new _observe_push_decision_state()'s HEAD lookup falls back to an empty string rather than raising on a nonzero git rev-parse exit code -- if this failed identically at both decision time and freshness time, two empty strings would spuriously compare equal as 'no drift'; no concrete reachable trigger was found (repositories capable of reaching this code path essentially always have a real, non-empty HEAD), and the realistic single-point-failure case (HEAD lookup fails only at freshness time) is independently confirmed to correctly report a mismatch, not a false match; (2) the pre-existing, unchanged _count_unpushed_commits() conflates 'true zero unpushed commits' with 'total git-command observation failure' via its own 0 fallback -- inherited from Section 13's pre-existing readiness computation (not introduced by 148G.1), contract-sanctioned (PBPC-REQ-042: '0 is a valid, meaningful value'), noted because 148G.1 newly relies on it for a security-relevant freshness comparison. PBPC-001 Section 18's missing 'broker construction failure' row independently classified as NON-NORMATIVE DOCUMENTATION DEBT -- DOES NOT BLOCK CERTIFICATION: PBPC-REQ-021 ('No fallback SHALL convert a broker evaluation failure, exception, or malformed result into a permission to push... SHALL fail closed') and Section 11's ownership table ('Broker-internal failure handling | Decision Consumption Point, treating any broker exception/malformed result as DENY-equivalent') are both worded generally enough to already normatively require construction-failure fail-closed behavior; Section 18's table is a worked-example matrix, not an exhaustive enumeration, and PBPC-REQ-063 only prohibits a listed category being owned by more than one component. No BLOCKING finding was identified. Regression: 79/79 (148G.1's own hardening suite + 148E/148F PBPC production-consumption suites + 148C.10 suite + the new 148G.2 suite, combined and independently re-run) + 422/422 (Foundation/PBPA suites) + 186/186 (runtime suites) + 186/186 (full push-suite regression across 8 files) + Fast Green (python -m pytest -m fast_green -n auto -q) 4391/4391 on a clean rerun (first run showed 4390 passed/1 failed in tests/test_backend_cli.py, a test entirely unrelated to push.py/Permission Broker with no relevant import, which passed both in isolation and on a full unmodified rerun of the same command -- pre-existing parallel-execution-order flakiness, not a regression, since this phase changed zero src/pcae/** files). Production diff: git diff --name-only <pre-148G.2>..HEAD -- src/pcae/ empty (this phase adds only a new test file and documentation, no production changes). Contract diff: git diff --name-only <pre-148G.2>..HEAD -- docs/contracts/ empty (PBPC-001 remains v1.2, PBPA-001 remains v1.0, both unamended). Verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- OPERATIONAL HARDENING CONFORMS. Chapter 148 certification readiness: READY FOR CHAPTER 148 CERTIFICATION WITH RETAINED NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS. Runtime reconfirmed Observed/observe/unavailable; IWC/AESIC/Runtime Enforcement independence reconfirmed unchanged; Prompt Generation (Phase 45F) remains DEFERRED, untouched. See docs/PHASE_148G.2_PERMISSION_BROKER_PRODUCTION_CONSUMPTION_OPERATIONAL_HARDENING_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md for full detail.
